newsitem.title: USA: Exxon says claims not false in premium gas ads.
newsitem.headline: Exxon says claims not false in premium gas ads.

text.p: Exxon Corp said Tuesday it made no false claims in advertising the benefits of its premium gasoline and said the Federal Trade Commission has agreed to scientific testing of the engine-cleaning capabilities of the fuel.

The statement follows an FTC announcement earlier Tuesday that Exxon and the U.S. agency have come to an out-of court settlement over what the FTC charges were overblown claims of the fuel's efficiency.

"The company's participation in this consent agreement is in no way an admission of wrongdoing and that the company maintains there was a sound basis for making its advertising claim," Exxon said in a statement.
But the FTC said that under the settlement Exxon must air television advertisements starting in September saying the right octane for most cars is regular octane.

In addition, the settlement requires that future advertising claiming premium gasoline allows car engines to run cleaner and more efficient than regular gasoline must be backed up with scientific evidence.
Exxon said the FTC has agreed for the first time to four specific tests to establish the engine-cleaning capability of Exxon's gasoline.
"Exxon is confident that its gasolines will pass these four specific tests," the statement said.
Exxon Senior Vice President called the agreement, which stems from an FTC lawsuit filed last September, as a "win-win solution" for both sides.

"We had been preparing to challenge the FTC in court over the issue, but our continuing dialogue with the Commission allowed both sides to identify areas of agreement," Exxon's R.L. Rich said in the statement.
"As a result of these discussions the FTC has recognized specific tests as standards for substantiation of these kinds of advertising claims, rather than arguing over opinions," he added.
((-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk 1212 859-1631))
